missing.item: Policy or a precise assumption establishing whether slashing must remain possible after an unstake matures
missing.why: The report’s PoC demonstrates that an operator can withdraw before a later slash request, but it does not establish that this violates the intended design. The README guidance described in the report leaves that policy question unresolved.
missing.resolves_when: Provide a cited contest or README clause requiring slashing to remain possible after the delay, or state the precise assumption under which the behavior is out of design.

missing.item: Evidence that the DSS could not slash before the unstake matured
missing.why: The control test shows a slash succeeds when requested one second earlier, so the demonstrated loss depends on the DSS losing a timing race.
missing.resolves_when: Demonstrate a scenario in which a cooldown, veto window, or other condition prevents an earlier slash request.

reason: The PoC resolves reachability and claim-specific reproduction: finalizing first makes the slash request revert and allows withdrawal. The control test shows the ordering matters. Whether this contradicts intended design remains unresolved, so the claim is not ready.
caps: severity medium capped: evidence impact is informational

evidence.claim: Operator pre-schedules an unstake, then finalizes it before the DSS's requestSlashing, so the slash reverts with VaultNotStakedToDSS and the operator escapes slashing.
evidence.support_reason: requestSlashing validates isVaultStakeToDSS (SlasherLib.sol:51-52); finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS (Core.sol:146-153) removes the vault from vaultStakedInDssMap (Operator.sol:103-108) after only MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY, with no DSS veto (finish hook ignoreFailure:true, Operator.sol:128; request hook ignoreFailure for unstake, Operator.sol:82). Nothing blocks the operator from finalizing before the DSS's slash request.
preconditions: Operator controls a vault staked to the DSS and has queued an unstake that has passed MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY
Operator can land finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS before the DSS's requestSlashing transaction

missing_evidence.item: Contest policy / README statement that slashing must remain possible after an unstake request matures, or that this ordering is not intended design
missing_evidence.why: The README explicitly says a DSS should stop counting a queued-unstake vault and that 'sitting on a queued withdraw doesn't provide an operator any edge'; the report itself concedes this may be intended design. Without a policy clause or precise assumption that slashing must survive the delay, the claim collides with the stated design intent.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A cited README/contest clause or sponsor statement says slashing must remain possible after MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY, or the report refutes the 'no edge' sentence for the slashing case.

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the DSS could not have slashed earlier (i.e., the operator's exit is not simply the DSS missing its window)
missing_evidence.why: The report's own control test shows the slash succeeds if requested one second earlier, so the effect is a timing race the DSS can win; this weakens severity but does not break the reachability of the evasion path.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A scenario where the DSS cannot request slashing before the unstake matures (e.g., slashing cooldown or veto window forces the ordering) is shown.
